To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) cyclins, cyclin-dependent kinas(es), and Cdk-inhibitors, which regulate cell proliferation, may function as oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes, (b) p53 and pRb, which function in the regulation of cell proliferation and apoptosis, may also be involved in tumor progression, and (c) detection of mutations of TP53 and/or RB and altered expression of TP53 and pRB may be of clinical significance.

(1) cyclins and cyclins-dependent kinases are oncogenic; (2) cyclin kinase inhibitors are tumor suppressor genes; (3) p53 and p53-regulatory genes are tumor suppressor; and (4) RB is also a tumor suppressor gene.
mutations and overexpression of cell cycle regulators, including p53, pRB and cyclins, are involved in the pathogenesis of neoplastic diseases and that they are clinically significant.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of cell cycle deregulation and the potential clinical implications for human cancer.
the molecular biology of the cell cycle and the role of its regulatory proteins in human cancer, with a particular focus on the RB and p53 tumor suppressor genes.

the molecular biology of cell cycle control and tumor suppressor genes, with the goal of understanding how these proteins function in cell cycle regulation and how their alterations contribute to the development of cancer and to the progression of neoplastic disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the molecular networking between cell cycle regulators, such as the cyclin-cdk complexes, the Cdk inhibitors, p53, and pRB is being unraveled.
mutations of cell cycle regulators are of clinical significance in human neoplastic diseases, and that they may be of potential use in cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and gene therapy.

the cell cycle is a complex and dynamic process, which is regulated by a number of proteins and complexes, and that the deregulation of these molecules may lead to the uncontrolled cell growth characteristic of neoplastic diseases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
mutations and altered expression in the cell cycle regulators are common in human cancers and may have prognostic value.
the cell cycle machinery is the most frequently altered pathway in human tumors.
cell cycle regulators are key molecules for tumor development.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell cycle machinery is a complex network of proteins, which is tightly regulated.
mutations of the RB gene are a common feature of human cancer and that these mutations can be detected by molecular genetic techniques in the majority of cases.
cell cycle control is a dynamic process involving multiple proteins that interact with one another.
